Ukrainian drones deliver new batch of food to Russian-occupied Oleshky

Reuters

04 October, 2026 10:30 pm IST

KYIV, Oct 4 (Reuters) – Ukraine’s military has again used drones to deliver food and medicines to the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine, Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said on Sunday.

Oleshky, a frontline town on the Dnipro River, which separates Russian and Ukrainian forces, has been under Russian occupation since 2022.

“For months, Russia has been trying to isolate Ukrainians in Oleshky from the outside world, even obstructing the delivery of food to people facing severe shortages,” Sybiha said on X.

Show Full Article

Ukraine used heavy-lift drones to deliver food and medicines to Oleshky at the end of September.

Sybiha said that the latest delivery consisted of nearly 400 packages containing almost 4 metric tons of food and medicine.

Ukrainian human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets told Ukrainian media last month that Russia had not agreed to Ukrainian proposals to allow civilians to evacuate from Oleshky.

The Kremlin said that Oleshky had critical problems with food and medicine supplies, but that Russia’s military was working to resolve them.

(Reporting by Pavel Polityuk; Editing by Emelia Sithole-Matarise)

Government forces seize capital of Ethiopia’s Tigray region from rebels

Reuters

04 October, 2026 02:00 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

Oct 4 (Reuters) – Ethiopian government forces and allied militias have regained control of the capital of Tigray, three sources told Reuters on Sunday, dealing a major setback to the opposition alliance that rules the northern region.

The Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF), which leads the opposition alliance, said in a statement posted on Facebook it had retreated from the capital and that the regional government would be “temporarily moved out of Mekelle and operate from somewhere else.”

A source close to the pro-government militia, the Tigray Peace Forces, said its fighters entered the centre of Mekelle on Saturday afternoon, followed by the Ethiopian military. A humanitarian source and a Mekelle resident, who asked not to be named, confirmed the city was controlled by government forces.

Show Full Article

The prime minister’s office did not respond immediately to a request for comment.

LOSS OF MEKELLE A MAJOR BLOW FOR TPLF

The taking of Mekelle by pro-government forces is a major loss for the opposition alliance led by the TPLF, which launched a big offensive on September 23 against the Ethiopian military.

Ethiopian federal forces and allied fighters have made a quick counterattack into Tigray, but analysts say the fighting — the worst escalation since a 2020-2022 civil war — threatens to escalate into a wider regional conflict.

The federal government in Addis Ababa severed diplomatic ties with Eritrea last week, accusing it of supporting the rebel alliance alongside Sudan and Egypt. The three countries deny this.

(Reporting by Ammu Kannampillay; Editing by Silvia Aloisi and Helen Popper)

Trump’s new ‘Super Intelligence’ task force will study AI risks, submit report in 4 months, WSJ says

The task force will be led by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, the Wall Street Journal reported, adding that he confirmed his role to the paper.

Maria Paula

04 October, 2026 01:58 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Jay Clayton

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

A new White House task force will produce a report assessing risks posed by artificial intelligence and what responsibility the US federal government should have over the technology.

The task force will be led by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, the Wall Street Journal reported, adding he confirmed his role to the paper. It makes Clayton effectively the Trump administration’s new AI czar, a senior White House official told the Wall Street Journal.

“The president asked that a group be put together that was going to ensure exactly what he said, which is that we stay the leaders in superintelligence, and that the interests of the American people are put first,” the Journal cited Clayton as saying. A White House official confirmed the Journal report.

Show Full Article

Despite growing concerns about security risks posed by AI, President Donald Trump has spurned calls for new regulations. Instead, he has prioritized keeping the US ahead of China and backed a voluntary framework involving outside safety audits and stronger internal controls.

“We have a very big lead, and we’re going to keep our lead, and it’s a very positive thing,” the president said during a meeting with industry executives this week.

The task force has been named the “Super Intelligence Force,” Trump’s preferred name for AI, and will have 120 days to prepare the report, the report said.

Separately, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent criticized prominent AI leaders’ warnings about existential risks posed by the technology as alarmist and unhelpful, calling on the industry to police itself and produce solutions.

“It is the people at the labs who have to accept responsibility, and I agree with that,” Bessent said in an Axios interview published Saturday. “I think the labs have come around to that way of thinking, too.”

–With assistance from Kate Sullivan.

(Adds White House response in third paragraph)
